The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Crypto Long & Short: The GENIUS Act’s guarantees don’t cover DeFi lending. Institutions weighing DeFi lending tend to ask which markets are safest. Mike Hathaway and Joseph Quintilian of Ajna argue the better question is who can change a loan’s terms after the money is lent, and why a fully backed stablecoin offers no protection against a token vote or a faulty price feed. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

OKXICE to debut tokenized stock trading with Strategy, Coinbase, Circle this month. After initial issuer pushback, the blockchain venue is set to start trading on Nov. 23 and said will list over 70 assets, including Strategy’s common and preferred shares and 59 of Direxion's ETFs. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Meet Spiko, the largest tokenized fund in the world you’ve probably never heard about. The firm’s flagship Spiko Amundi Overnight Swap Fund (SAFO) held $2.39 billion in assets under management as of late last month. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Live news: Bitcoin remains under pressure as CoreWeave, Nvidia lead AI rebound. The DRAM ETF jumps 8% and semiconductor stocks gain more than 4%, while bitcoin continues to test its 200-day moving average. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin barely flinches at hot CPI as ETF selling slows. Your day-ahead look for Nov. 11, 2026 Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin sits out stock rebound as ETF outflows extend to fourth day. Bitcoin held steady near $74,000 as Tuesday's hot inflation figure lifted the odds on a U.S. interest-rate increase to around 90%. ETF outflows extended to a fourth day and liquidations jumped. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $74,521 with a +1.46% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $2,080.81 with a +1.61% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Bitcoin and Blockchain Basics

items.title: Cryptocurrency Regulation: A Guide to U.S. & Global Policies | Britannica Money
items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established the first federal regulatory framework for stablecoins in the United States. It limits who can issue stablecoins and requires issuers to maintain reserves backing the tokens they have issued, make monthly disclosures detailing the assets held in reserve, and comply with anti–money laundering and consumer protection requirements.

### What is the CLARITY Act? [...] United Kingdom. The U.K. began regulating cryptocurrency in 2020. In October 2023, the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) introduced stricter rules on crypto advertising. The Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 also expanded oversight of stablecoins. A broader regulatory framework was approved in 2026 and is scheduled to take effect in October 2027, bringing activities including crypto trading, custody, staking, and stablecoin issuance under FCA oversight.

items.description:
The Forum came at a consequential juncture. After four years of an AI-driven bull market, markets have largely priced in the new regime of structurally higher interest rates we’ve talked about for five years. That makes the investment outlook less directional and more nuanced. Discussions ranged from shifting global capital flows and changing relationships between stocks, bonds and currencies to investment opportunities across Europe, China and emerging markets. Participants also explored how [...] grade (IG) returns are denominated in U.S. dollars, and the rest in local currencies. Indexes or prices used are: spot Brent crude, ICE U.S. Dollar Index (DXY), spot gold, spot bitcoin, MSCI Emerging Markets Index, MSCI Europe Index, LSEG Datastream 10-year benchmark government bond index (U.S., Germany and Italy), Bloomberg Global High Yield Index, J.P. Morgan EMBI Index, Bloomberg Global Corporate Index and MSCI USA Index. [...] 3: Eyeing rates

We’ve long expected rates to stay structurally higher. At the forum, the focus was on what that means for markets and portfolios. Shifting capital flows, changing correlations between stocks, bonds and currencies could create new sources of volatility and challenge traditional portfolio hedges. That makes staying flexible key to navigating risks and seizing opportunities.
